title: Isolated rental-style subscription and upgrade-velocity study for Private/VPC packaging
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Run a small-scale experiment to validate a rental-style subscription (time-limited capacity bundles) and an explicit upgrade-velocity policy for Private/VPC/on-prem customers. The goal is to provide an alternative to fixed multi-year commit bands that lowers sales friction, gives customers predictable short-term costs, and preserves upgrade cadence guarantees for critical patches. Outcomes should feed pricing playbook, sales one-pagers, and the security questionnaire responses for enterprise RFIs.
background: Sales and pre-sales teams report 3 common objections for Private/VPC deals: (1) multi-year seat or commit bands are hard to forecast for pilot customers; (2) customers want guaranteed upgrade windows and a documented emergency patch SLA; (3) security/RFIs require clear entitlements and a patch cadence note. This experiment pairs a time-bound rental SKU with upgrade-velocity tiers (Standard, Accelerated, Emergency) and tests how those map to acceptable pricing and support credits.
goals: Validate willingness-to-pay for 6/12-month rental bundles vs. 1-3 year commit bands
Define upgrade-velocity tiers and emergency patch SLAs that legal/security can sign off on
Produce standardized language for security questionnaires describing entitlements, KMS/HSM options, and upgrade windows
out_of_scope: Full legal contract rework; large enterprise custom RFAs beyond templated SQ language; Dedicated capacity reserved multi-year pricing changes.
approach: We will run 6 sales trials with prospective customers (mid-market to enterprise) offering a rental SKU priced at ~1.5x monthly equivalent of our baseline commit price with optional ops credits. For each interested buyer we will capture: deal signal, explicit objection handling notes, requested upgrade cadence, and security questionnaire items. Internally we will create a draft patch schedule (Standard=quarterly, Accelerated=monthly, Emergency=72hrs) and map support credit buckets to those tiers. Iterate with Security/Legal in two review passes.
acceptance_criteria: Three signed trial agreements using the rental SKU OR three documented sales objections with pricing delta >15%
Security/Legal approval of the upgrade-velocity language and emergency patch SLA draft
Draft SQ text (answers) covering entitlements, KMS options, logging/audit, and upgrade windows committed to the Confluence playbook
Playbook page with clear guidance for Sales on quoting rental SKU and selecting support tier
deliverables: Pricing matrix for 6/12 month rental bundles (spreadsheet link)
Upgrade-velocity policy doc (Standard/Accelerated/Emergency) with SLOs and support credit mapping
Sales one-pager and quoting macros for Redwood Console and Contract team
risks: Customers may prefer traditional multi-year discounts, reducing conversion from trials
Emergency patch SLA could materially increase operational load without commensurate pricing uplift
Legal may require escrow or longer notice periods that undermine rental flexibility
tradeoffs: We trade lower entry friction (rental SKU) against potentially higher churn and more frequent upgrade windows to manage. We prefer to keep financial exposure low for Redwood by pricing rental slightly above pro-rated commit equivalents and using ops credits as a gating mechanism for accelerated/emergency tiers.
